exam: TNPSC Group II / IIA · General English
scope: General English Q1–100, adapted from TNPSC’s numbered specimen. The shared e-Sevai passage appears with Q62–64. Q93 was referred to an expert committee.

questionCandidates.text: Which benefit can a business gain by preparing for future changes?
What is the term for senators prolonging a debate to delay a proposal and pressure the majority to abandon it?
What does ‘matronymic’ mean?

options.A: A name derived from the mother’s name
options.C: A name taken from a famous person

questionCandidates.text:
Which expressions in ‘Sea Fever’ evoke sound?
1. Wheels kick  2. Seagulls cry  3. Clouds flying  4. Running tide  5. Sails shaking  6. Wind’s song

Match the words with their synonyms.
(a) Champing  (b) Perplexing  (c) Thronging  (d) Hearkening
1. Confusing  2. Listening, heading  3. Munching, chewing  4. Crowding

Match each word with its synonym.
(a) Mourn  (b) Veil  (c) Crown  (d) Quest
1. Pinnacle  2. Search  3. Anguish  4. Conceal

Which statements agree with Nadia Bush’s account?
1. The house looks alive in daylight.
2. The poet often feels tempted to enter it.
3. A tree stands beside the house.
4. The tree is growing faster.

Supply the five missing words in order. Children like to ___ crispy snacks. The author in ‘Seventeen Oranges’ was fond of ___ oranges. He was eventually forced to ___ all the ___, including ___.
1. eating  2. swallow  3. munch  4. pips  5. chunks

Consider these statements about Jawaharlal Nehru.
(i) He wrote ‘Glimpses of Indian History’.
(ii) He was India’s first prime minister.
(iii) He is regarded as the architect of the modern Indian nation-state.
Which are true?

Match each subject to its paired word.
(a) Walls  (b) Lights  (c) People  (d) Path of a valley  (e) Insects
1. Straggle  2. Flicker  3. Scuttle  4. Crumble  5. Huddle

Which statements about ‘The Tempest’ are true?
(i) Shakespeare wrote it in 1500.
(ii) It is among his last plays.
(iii) A real shipwreck is believed to have inspired it.
Choose the English translation of ‘நாளை இந்நேரத்திற்குள் நான் இந்த வேலையை முடித்திருப்பேன்.’

options.A: I will have completed this work by tomorrow.
options.B: I would have finished this work by tomorrow.
options.C: I have completed this work by this time tomorrow.
options.D: I would have completed this work by this time tomorrow.

questionCandidates.text:
Which Tamil sentence conveys ‘They were being followed when they left the building’?
(a) அவர்கள் கட்டிடத்தை விட்டு வெளியேறிய போது அவர்களை பின் தொடர்ந்தார்கள்.
(b) அவர்கள் கட்டிடத்தை விட்டு வெளியேறும் போது அவர்கள் பின் தொடரப்பட்டுக் கொண்டிருந்தார்கள்.
(c) அவர்கள் கட்டிடத்தை விட்டு வெளியேறினார்கள், அவர்களை பின் தொடர்ந்தார்கள்.
(d) அவர்கள் கட்டிடத்தை விட்டு வெளியேறும் போது அவர்கள் பின் தொடர்ந்தார்கள்.

Passage summary — Aadhaar began in welfare delivery and expanded into other services. Its goals include preventing fraud and widening access to finance. Privacy and exclusion remain concerns, and courts weigh security against rights.
Which statements reflect the passage?
(a) Its only use is welfare distribution.  (b) Its use has expanded.  (c) Reducing fraud and increasing financial inclusion were aims.  (d) There are privacy and exclusion concerns.

Passage summary — Banks hope for stronger growth in 2025. Government steps to revive industry and RBI measures to help banks restructure are behind this optimism. Which issue does the question identify as the largest challenge for Indian banks?

options.C: The rising level of non-performing assets

questionCandidates.text: Which type of question draws attention to an idea or illustrates a point?

Passage summary — As market share falls, a CEO considers price cuts or a niche product. The CEO sees discounts as temporary relief that could harm the brand, and favours distinctive products and service to retain customers. Which inference is supported?
(a) Short-term gains come first.  (b) The CEO values sustainable growth and loyalty.  (c) Production capacity is the main problem.  (d) The niche strategy has already succeeded.

Passage summary — Tamil Nadu’s climate mission describes restoring forests to absorb carbon and support biodiversity, protecting coasts against higher seas, expanding solar and wind power, and helping communities adapt. Match initiatives to outcomes.
(a) Reforestation  (b) Coastal zone management  (c) Renewable energy  (d) Community adaptation
1. Less reliance on fossil fuels  2. Greater local resilience  3. More carbon absorption and biodiversity  4. Shoreline protection

Passage summary — Cryptocurrency and traditional stocks are investments. Crypto prices are described as more volatile. Both react to market fluctuations in different ways. Which statements follow?
(a) Neither involves investment.  (b) Both involve investment.  (c) Both are immune to fluctuations.  (d) They react differently to fluctuations.

Passage summary — Heating water brings it to the boil, produces steam and is followed by cooling and condensation. Which statements preserve the sequence?
(a) Steam appears before boiling.  (b) Heating precedes boiling.  (c) Steam cools and condenses after it forms.  (d) The process starts with cooling steam.

Passage summary — Reforestation restores damaged ecosystems, supports biodiversity, improves air and helps land retain water. Which claims support its benefits?
(a) It reduces biodiversity.  (b) It restores damaged ecosystems.  (c) It improves air quality.  (d) It increases water retention.
Which feature is out of place in a formal letter?

Put the statements about contemporary art into a logical order.
(a) This shift challenges the purpose of artistic expression.
(b) An interdisciplinary approach characterises contemporary art.
(c) The boundaries between different artistic connections appear to have merged.
(d) As a result, artists are exploring new kinds of creative collaboration.

Order P, Q, R and S between the given opening and closing statements.
S1. Intellectual history offers insight into the development of human history.
P. This, however, considers the historical context in which ideas emerged.
Q. Intellectual history traces major concepts and their influence on society.
R. Consequently, interpretations can differ with each researcher’s perspective.
S. Moreover, the concepts are revisited and reinterpreted over time.
S6. It seeks to illuminate how ideas intersect with their social and cultural setting.

options.A: S1, S, Q, P, R, S6
options.B: S1, Q, S, R, P, S6
options.C: S1, R, P, Q, S, S6
options.D: S1, P, S, Q, R, S6

questionCandidates.text: Moderates, liberals, radicals and socialists pursued different strands of the freedom struggle in colonial India. Which inference best follows?

options.A: Nationalism in colonial India led to independence.
options.B: Indian nationalism arose in a colonial context.

questionCandidates.text:
Choose the sequence of adjectives that completes all four sentences.
1. The manager’s positive decisions often produced an ___ result.
2. The chef’s dish was ___ in taste and elaborately presented.
3. The chief guest’s speech was so ___ that the audience left motivated.
4. The student used ___ evidence that made the project’s outcome predictable.

Which examples use ‘right’ in its legal sense?
(a) Turn right at the next intersection.  (b) It is your right to remain silent.  (c) The answer is right in front of you.  (d) He wanted to right the wrong he did to his sister.
Which pair consists of homophones?

Complete the phrasal verbs in order.
1. Ring her ___ and say you will be late.
2. Drop ___ for tea when you pass by.
3. If you cannot afford it, you must do ___ it.
4. Try the car ___ on the road before buying it.
(a) out  (b) in  (c) up  (d) without
Which spelling denotes the social class associated in the question with money and a higher position in society?

Which British and American English pairs are incorrectly matched?
1. Courgette – Egg plant  2. Rocket – Arugala  3. Aubergine – Zucchini  4. Fringe – Bangs

Which compound-word types are incorrectly paired with their examples?
1. Open compound – snowman  2. Closed compound – ice cream  3. Co-ordinative compound – walkie-talkie  4. Adjective compound – blue-eyed
A comparison says that life is ‘like’ a pathless wood. What figure of speech is used?

Which passive forms preserve the meaning of ‘The Manager will give you a ticket’?
(a) A ticket will be given to the Manager by you.
(b) A ticket will be given to you by the Manager.
(c) The Manager will be given a ticket by you.
(d) You will be given a ticket by the Manager.

Match each example with its sentence type.
(a) This pen is blue.  (b) Please help me.  (c) How are you?  (d) How well she dances!
1. Interrogative  2. Exclamatory  3. Declarative  4. Imperative
Change ‘Is she not changing her dress?’ into a statement.

options.A: She will not change her dress.
options.B: She was not changing her dress.
options.D: She is not changing her dress.

questionCandidates.text: Select the negative transformation of ‘He is too shrewd to be cheated’.

options.A: He is not shrewd enough to be cheated.
options.B: He is so shrewd that he cannot be cheated.
options.C: He is not too shrewd to be cheated.

questionCandidates.text: Which assertive form expresses ‘Had she known it earlier!’?

options.B: I wish she had known it earlier.
options.D: She should have known it earlier.

questionCandidates.text: Which sentence uses the infinitive correctly?

options.A: She is bold enough to take decisions.
options.B: She is bold enough in accepting challenges.
options.C: She is bold but afraid of snakes.
options.D: She is bold enough to taking decisions.

questionCandidates.text: In ‘I heard of his having gained a prize’, what is the grammatical form of ‘having gained’?
Identify the participle in ‘The barking dog kept the neighbours awake all night’.
Supply the question tag. ‘Let’s all go to the beach this evening, ______’
Which combination of ‘The company decreased its product prices’ and ‘Sales increased gradually’ best expresses cause and effect?

options.A: The company decreased its product prices, which caused sales to increase gradually.
options.B: The company decreased its product prices, so sales increased gradually.
options.C: The company decreased its product prices and sales increased gradually.
options.D: Sales increased gradually as a result of the company decreasing its product prices.

questionCandidates.text: Which sentence uses an apostrophe to show possession?

options.B: Mr. X’s new bag is ready.

questionCandidates.text: What defines an ad hoc committee?

options.B: It disbands once its specific task is finished.
options.D: It supervises every activity of the organisation.

questionCandidates.text: What is an agenda?

options.C: A list of matters for discussion

questionCandidates.text: In which year did the Tamil Nadu Physical Education and Sports University start functioning?
Which meaning best fits ‘repercussion’?
Which element is usually absent from a memo?
Which salutation suits a formal letter?
What does DGTD stand for?

Which works are poems by Robert Frost?
1. The Road Not Taken  2. The Jungle Book  3. Mending Wall  4. Treasure Island

Which statements conflict with Gieve Patel’s ‘On Killing a Tree’?
1. Felling a tree is likened to murder.  2. A single stab of a knife will cut the tree.  3. The poet disapproves of humanity’s failure to care for the earth.  4. The tree draws its strength from its large branches.
A verse describes something as swifter than a cheetah, with a tail stretching for miles, larger than a mountain and very strong. Which figure of speech do the options identify?

Which aims are associated with Navika Sagar Parikrama?
1. Improve women’s economic status.  2. Enable women to achieve their potential.  3. Promote reservation for women in the Indian Navy.  4. Encourage ocean sailing.

Who inspired Arthur Conan Doyle’s Sherlock Holmes?
(a) Dr. Watson  (b) Dr. Ainstree  (c) Inspector Smith  (d) Joseph Bell

Which descriptions of Alfred Nobel are incorrect?
1. He was called Europe’s richest vagabond.  2. He was a chemist, engineer and aspiring poet.  3. He felt guilty about inventing destructive things.  4. He felt guilty about earning so much money.

Which statements about Mithali Dorai Raj are incorrect?
1. She was the first to score seven consecutive centuries.  2. Tamil is her mother tongue.  3. She received the Padma Bhushan.  4. She is known as the ‘Tendulkar of Indian Women’s Cricket’.  5. Her family did not encourage her to play cricket.
Choose the English translation of ‘பறவைகள் பறக்கின்றன’.
What is the name for a word-for-word translation?
Which English expression corresponds to ‘தூண்டிவிடாதே’?

options.D: Don’t make me do what I don’t want to.

questionCandidates.text:
Passage summary for Q62–64 — Tamil Nadu’s e-Sevai centres streamline access to government services such as birth certificates and land records. Links to state databases reduce delays and aim to improve transparency. Service quality varies. Rural digital literacy, trained staff, continued investment and reliable infrastructure all affect the initiative’s long-term success.

What primary function does the passage assign to e-Sevai centres?

options.A: Provide free internet access in rural areas
options.C: Train government staff in digital literacy

questionCandidates.text:
Passage summary for Q62–64 — Tamil Nadu’s e-Sevai centres streamline access to government services such as birth certificates and land records. Links to state databases reduce delays and aim to improve transparency. Service quality varies. Rural digital literacy, trained staff, continued investment and reliable infrastructure all affect the initiative’s long-term success.

What does the passage identify as essential to the long-term success of e-Sevai?

options.A: Increasing the number of physical centres
options.C: Closing the digital divide and maintaining dependable infrastructure
options.D: Reducing the range of online services

questionCandidates.text:
Passage summary for Q62–64 — Tamil Nadu’s e-Sevai centres streamline access to government services such as birth certificates and land records. Links to state databases reduce delays and aim to improve transparency. Service quality varies. Rural digital literacy, trained staff, continued investment and reliable infrastructure all affect the initiative’s long-term success.

What does ‘streamline’ mean in this passage?
Which question elicits ‘He has gone to the railway station to see off his cousin’?

options.A: Why has he gone to the railway station?
options.B: Why he went to the railway station?
options.C: Why he go to the railway station?
options.D: Why have he gone to the railway station?

questionCandidates.text:
Passage summary — Unreliable internet and scarce devices affect schools and businesses in a rural community. Leaders suggest a shared digital centre, but residents worry about surveillance and misuse of data. Which statements follow?
(a) The digital divide is mainly urban.  (b) The community faces economic and educational disadvantages.  (c) Everyone agrees about the proposed centre.  (d) Privacy concerns complicate efforts to close the divide.
Passage summary — Dr. Montague describes women as equal in intelligence to men and attributes to them an intuitive ability to grasp a problem as a whole. Which subject best captures the passage?
Passage summary — At an annual school science fair, many students investigated environmental issues. Judges rewarded creativity and scientific accuracy. Which statement follows?

options.D: The fair takes place every two years.

questionCandidates.text:
Passage summary — A train clanks along the line, steam forms a white cloud, passengers watch the scenery and the whistle gives a long, mournful note. Match descriptions with their effects.
(a) Rhythmic clanting  (b) Steam billows  (c) Passengers gazing  (d) Mournful whistle
1. Creates a visual effect  2. Provides an auditory experience  3. Highlights the pace of the train  4. Indicates observation and travel
He is at the ______ in the organisation.
______, I was born on exactly the same day as my wife.

Passage summary — Online government services improve access, reduce delays and can make processes more transparent and efficient, building public trust. Which inferences follow?
(a) E-governance increases delays.  (b) It can increase transparency.  (c) Simpler processes can build trust.  (d) Digital platforms reduce access.

Passage summary — Renewables can reduce carbon emissions. Wind and solar power are increasingly viable, and sustainable energy matters for future generations. Which statements capture these points?
(a) Renewables have no effect on climate change.  (b) They lower carbon emissions.  (c) Wind and solar are becoming more viable.  (d) Sustainable energy is vital for future generations.

A volunteer emails the coordinator of a local charity for an updated list of items needed as donations. How would this query be classified?
(a) Charity Support Inquiry  (b) Material Request  (c) Donation Item Request  (d) Volunteer co-ordination
Complete the reply. ‘You want to see him? ______’
What kind of question is ‘Will you tell me who is there?’
A woman reads a message and sighs. Which feeling does her reaction suggest?
A celebrity visits a local bookshop without wanting to be recognised. Which word describes the visit?
Chuck is described as ‘mendacious’ about his vegetarianism. Which word is closest in meaning to ‘mendacious’?

A driver is described in terms of his ‘cautiousness’ and his ‘innate’ talent. Choose antonyms for the two words, in order.
(a) Gloomy, active  (b) Dim, retain  (c) Recklessness, acquired  (d) Subtle, intolerant

A civil servant must explain climate initiatives to the public. Which collocations best suit that purpose?
(a) Spread climate misinformation.  (b) Raise public awareness about climate impacts.  (c) Minimise the urgency of climate action.  (d) Engage in stakeholder consultations.

Which idioms are incorrectly paired with their meanings?
1. To brow beat – bully  2. To be at large – to blame each other  3. To knit the brow – to frown  4. To pass the buck – free
The pupil was asked to ______ the mistake.
Which single word denotes a creature with both male and female reproductive organs?
Choose the forms that express the opposites of ‘consistent’ and ‘embark’, respectively.
What does IPCC stand for?
What part of speech is ‘rather’ in ‘He makes rather a fuss about ordinary things’?
Which sentence is grammatically correct?

options.A: The wages of sin are death.
options.B: His wages is Rs. 1,000 a day.

questionCandidates.text: Supply the verb forms. ‘She ______ (is) tired because she ______ (clean) the house yesterday.’
Which sentence is imperative?

options.B: How did you explain this question?

questionCandidates.text: Classify ‘Let my head be shattered to pieces’.
Turn ‘You should answer all the questions’ into an imperative.

options.A: Should you answer all the questions?

questionCandidates.text: Choose the interrogative form offered for ‘You have to be there on Monday’.

options.A: Will you be there on Monday?
options.B: Would you be there on Monday?
options.C: Can you be there on Monday?
options.D: Could you be there on Monday?

issues: TNPSC referred this question and its answer to an expert committee.

questionCandidates.text: Which choice recasts ‘Give me a book’ as an appreciative statement?

options.A: I’m glad that you have given a book.
options.B: Thank you for giving a book.
options.C: I appreciate you giving a book.
options.D: Why do you not give a book?

questionCandidates.text: Dogs usually ______ cats.
If she had studied well, she ______ in the examination.
Classify the sentence ‘He commented how beautiful the girl was’.
Classify the phrase as presented in ‘A crown made of gold’.
Which set gives three structures for the positive degree of comparison?
Which sentence uses the comparative degree correctly?

options.A: He is more smarter than any one in the class.
options.B: This bus is less more crowded than the other.
options.C: This sum is less complicated than the previous one.
options.D: The game is more easier than expected.
